title: Wellness Membership Sessions and Covered Therapy
content:
Wellness Membership sessions are wellness services, not therapy billed to a payer.

## Principle

Membership sessions are wellness services: while the member holds an Insured Plan of Care or a Workers' Compensation Referral in active status, maintenance sessions are not booked, because they would duplicate skilled therapy billed to a payer; gym and pool access continue.

## What the principle covers

- **Maintenance sessions** of the Wellness Membership are not booked for the whole time the member holds an Insured Plan of Care in active status, or a Workers' Compensation Referral in active status.
- **Gym and pool access** included in the member's tier continue during that time.
- The status that decides it is the status of the Insured Plan of Care or the Workers' Compensation Referral in the company's records for the same person who holds the Wellness Membership.

## Table of the principle

| Member holds an Insured Plan of Care in active status | Member holds a Workers' Compensation Referral in active status | Maintenance sessions booked | Gym and pool access of the tier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | No | No | continue |
| No | Yes | No | continue |
| Yes | Yes | No | continue |

## Hypothetical illustration

A Wellness Plus Membership member, whose tier includes maintenance sessions, the gym and the pool, opens an Insured Plan of Care for a new injury. While that plan of care is in active status, no maintenance session is booked on the membership; the member keeps using the gym and the pool.
